name: Multi-Index Monte Carlo: the MIMC complexity theorem (Giles 2015, Theorem 2)

milestones.title: §2.4 — cross-differences telescope over boxes
milestones.description: With $\Delta_d P_{\boldsymbol\ell}\equiv P_{\boldsymbol\ell}-P_{\boldsymbol\ell-\mathbf e_d}$ and the cross-difference $\boldsymbol\Delta P_{\boldsymbol\ell}\equiv\big(\prod_{d=1}^D\Delta_d\big)P_{\boldsymbol\ell}$ (with $P\equiv0$ at indices with a negative entry), the cross-differences telescope: $\sum_{\boldsymbol\ell\le\mathbf k}\boldsymbol\Delta P_{\boldsymbol\ell}=P_{\mathbf k}$ for every $\mathbf k\in\mathbb N^D$ (Giles 2015, §2.4, p. 13; the finite form of the telescoping sum).

milestones.title: §2.4 — the telescoping sum $\mathbb{E}[P]=\sum_{\boldsymbol\ell\ge\mathbf 0}\mathbb{E}[\boldsymbol\Delta P_{\boldsymbol\ell}]$
milestones.description: Under condition i) and $|\mathbb{E}[\boldsymbol\Delta P_{\boldsymbol\ell}]|\le c_1 2^{-\boldsymbol\alpha\cdot\boldsymbol\ell}$ with $\alpha_d>0$ (conditions ii) and iii) of Theorem 2), the series $\sum_{\boldsymbol\ell\in\mathbb N^D}\mathbb{E}[\boldsymbol\Delta P_{\boldsymbol\ell}]$ converges absolutely and its sum is $\mathbb{E}[P]$ (Giles 2015, §2.4, p. 13: "the telescoping sum becomes $\mathbb{E}[P]=\sum_{\boldsymbol\ell\ge0}\mathbb{E}[\boldsymbol\Delta P_{\boldsymbol\ell}]$").

milestones.title: Theorem 2 — the case $\alpha_d>\tfrac12\beta_d$, with the paper's exponents
milestones.description: When $\alpha_d>\tfrac12\beta_d$ for every $d$, the bound of Theorem 2 holds with the exponents stated in the paper, $e_1=2D_2$ and $e_2=(D_2-1)(2+\eta)$ (Giles 2015, §2.4, Theorem 2, pp. 13–14).

milestones.title: Theorem 2 — explicit exponents when some $\alpha_d=\tfrac12\beta_d$
milestones.description: For $\alpha_d\ge\tfrac12\beta_d$, where the paper notes that "the form of the exponents is more complicated when $\alpha_d=\tfrac12\beta_d$ for some $d$" and states none, the bound holds with $e_1=2D_2+(D_3-3)^+$ and $e_2=(D_2-1)(2+\eta)+(D_3-1)^+$, where $D_3=\#\{d:\alpha_d=\tfrac12\beta_d\}$ and $x^+=\max(x,0)$. These exponents are this formalization's (they reduce to the paper's when $D_3=0$) and are not claimed to be sharp.
